Peak Pro profiles
Live boost
The Peak’s real Boost command, sent to the running cycle. Only available while a cycle is active.
Next-cycle adjustments
Saves a +15-second duration or +15°F target for the selected profile. These change the next cycle, not the running one.
connection details
No UUID is needed. Emberwatch checks the known Peak Pro control services automatically after you select your device.
Dr. Dabber Switch 2
Sends the two commands the Dr. Dabber app was watched issuing — the state frame and the clock — and nothing else. Decode and provenance in docs/dr-dabber-switch2-frames.md.

frames0
No preset target seen yet — it arrives in an a3 frame, not in the state frame.
Frame
Every byte of the last state frame. A byte that just changed lights up; click one to read what it is.
Control
Log
Repeated frames collapse. Any frame that differs from the one before it prints in full with the changed bytes named, which is where the protocol is.
raw write
This sends bytes straight to the heater's control characteristic. It is here because decoding b5 needs it and there is no other way to get it. Type the payload only — the opcode, the length and the trailing opcode are added for you. Nothing sends until it is armed.
Replay a capture
Paste a log — from here, from the sniffer, from anywhere. Lines of hex go through the same decode a live notification takes; anything else becomes a mark, so labels stay next to the traffic they describe. Nothing is sent to the device.
device probe
Surveys any Bluetooth device: every service, every characteristic, its properties, and the current value of anything readable. It only reads — nothing is written to the device.
After the survey it subscribes to everything that can notify and prints what arrives for 20 seconds. Use the device while it listens — press a button, start a cycle, change a temperature — and its own traffic lands in the report. That is how a protocol gets read.
Extra service UUIDs
Web Bluetooth hides any service that was not named before the chooser opened, so an unknown device shows nothing until its UUIDs are listed here. Read them off chrome://bluetooth-internals → Devices → Inspect. Saved between sessions.
